transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I came in because... I know this is going to sound hard to explain, but I’ve been completely convinced lately that one of my MBA classmates and a startup advisor I know are quietly coordinating career opportunities for me. 

Like, I'll hear certain comments they make in class, or I'll read specific Slack messages, and I can just tell they are coded signals about where my career is supposed to go. It's been taking up a lot of my headspace, so I figured I should probably talk to someone about it.
Do you think it's possible that you're misinterpreting these comments and messages?

I mean, I guess logically it's possible? But... honestly, no, it doesn't feel like I'm misinterpreting them. Like I was just saying, I am just completely convinced that they are coordinating things behind the scenes for me. 

When I look at those Slack messages or hear what they say in class, the coded signals about my career just seem so obvious and real to me. It doesn't feel like a misunderstanding. I just can't shake the feeling that it's actually happening exactly the way I see it.
Have you ever had any doubts about this coordination happening behind the scenes?

Not really, no. I know I just said it's logically possible I could be misinterpreting things, but when it comes down to it... I don't really have any doubts. I'm completely convinced that this classmate and the startup advisor are quietly coordinating these opportunities for me. 

Every time I hear those comments in class or read those Slack messages, it just reinforces it. To me, they are definitely coded signals about where my career is supposed to go. I don't doubt it at all when it's happening.
Is this belief about your classmate and the startup advisor coordinating career opportunities for you part of a larger, organized plan that you've figured out?

Yeah, I mean... that's exactly what it feels like. Like I've been saying, it really feels like this whole organized thing that they've put together. 

I'm just so convinced that my classmate and the advisor are quietly coordinating these opportunities behind the scenes. All those things they say in class, or the specific Slack messages... they all fit together as these coded signals pointing to this specific path my career is supposed to take. So, yeah, it really does feel like a larger plan that I'm picking up on.
Is this belief about your classmate and the startup advisor coordinating career opportunities for you causing you any significant stress or problems in your daily life?

Yeah, it actually is starting to cause some issues. Um, at work, my manager has started documenting things... like missed handoffs and what they called unreliable follow-through on my end. And then at school, my professor actually questioned my judgment on a recent group assignment. 

I mean, I'm still showing up to everything—work and classes—but... my relationships in both places are definitely getting strained. It got to the point where they're strained enough that I felt I really needed to come in and get some help.
Is your belief about the coordinated career opportunities something that you think is only happening to you, or do you think it's part of something bigger that affects other people as well?

I really think it's just happening to me. Like I said when I first came in—and I know it sounds hard to explain to other people—but I've been completely convinced that this MBA classmate and the startup advisor are quietly coordinating these opportunities specifically for me. 

I don't think it's part of some massive thing affecting other students or anything like that. It's just... those certain comments in class or the Slack messages, I see them as coded signals specifically about where my career is supposed to go. So, yeah, I believe it's just focused on me and my path.
Do you think the beliefs you have about your classmate and the startup advisor are all connected and part of a single, coherent plan?

Yeah, I do. I mean, it all feels very connected. Like I was saying, I know it sounds really hard to explain, but I've just been so convinced that my classmate and the startup advisor are quietly coordinating all these opportunities for me. 

Every little thing—like the specific comments they make in class, or the messages they send on Slack—it all feels like part of one big, coherent plan. I see them as these coded signals that are all pointing toward where my career is supposed to go. So, yes, it definitely feels like it's all tied together in one single plan for me.
Would you describe the idea that your classmate and the startup advisor are sending you coded signals as strange or unusual to other people?

Yeah, I... I do know it sounds strange to other people. I mean, that's actually a big part of why I came in. I realize how hard it is to explain to anyone else. To me, I've just been so completely convinced that they're quietly coordinating these opportunities for me, and that those class comments or Slack messages are coded signals about my career path. But... I can definitely see how someone else looking at it would think it's unusual or hard to believe.
Do you think the coded signals you believe your classmate and the startup advisor are sending would seem bizarre or unbelievable to most people if you explained them in detail?

Yeah, I do think most people would find it unbelievable. Like I've been saying, I know it sounds really hard to explain to anyone else. If I sat down and tried to detail exactly how a specific Slack message or a random comment in class was actually a coded signal about my career... I know it would sound bizarre to them. But to me, I've just been so completely convinced that they are quietly coordinating these opportunities for me. It's real to me, even if I know how it sounds to everyone else.
Have you ever considered the possibility that your interpretation of these coded signals could be wrong, even if it feels very real to you?

I have tried to tell myself that, yeah. I mean, that's really why I came in to see you. I know this sounds so hard to explain, and I do try to step back and ask myself if I'm just reading into things. 

But... I've just been so completely convinced that my MBA classmate and that startup advisor are quietly coordinating these opportunities for me. It's like, no matter how much I try to rationalize it or doubt it, those certain comments in class or the Slack messages just feel exactly like coded signals about where my career is supposed to go. So, I do try to consider that I might be wrong, but it just hasn't shaken how absolutely real it feels when it happens.
Are you having difficulty interacting with your classmates or colleagues because of your beliefs about the coded signals?

Yeah, it is. I mean, I'm still showing up to work and my classes, but... things are definitely getting strained. At work, my manager has actually started documenting some missed handoffs and, um, what they called unreliable follow-through on my part. And then at school, my professor recently questioned my judgment on a group assignment. So, yeah, my relationships with my colleagues and classmates are getting strained enough that... well, that's really why I felt I needed to come in and get some help.
Are you experiencing significant emotional distress as a result of believing your classmate and the startup advisor are coordinating career opportunities for you?

No, not really. I wouldn't say I'm distressed by it. Honestly, it's more... confusing than anything else. Like, the belief itself that they're helping me isn't upsetting—if anything, it should be a good thing, right? It's just the fallout from it, like the issues at work and school, that's stressful. But the actual idea that they're sending me signals hasn't made me feel scared or upset.
Have your beliefs about the coded signals and career coordination been consistent since you first started noticing them?

Yeah, I think so. I mean, I haven't really noticed them changing or anything. Ever since I first picked up on it, it's just... it's just been the same feeling that they're guiding me. So, yeah, I'd say it's been pretty consistent. I haven't really tracked it day by day, but the belief hasn't really gone away or shifted.
Do you think there's a specific goal or outcome that your classmate and the startup advisor are trying to achieve through their coordination?

Well, I guess the specific goal is just... my career path. Like I mentioned, I've been completely convinced that this classmate and the startup advisor are quietly coordinating opportunities for me. It's hard to explain, but I really believe that certain comments they make in class, or even specific Slack messages, are actually coded signals. And those signals are pointing me toward where my career is supposed to go. So, the goal seems to be guiding my professional future.
Have you ever had a period of time where you didn't believe your classmate and the startup advisor were coordinating career opportunities for you?

Yeah, definitely. I mean, before this recent stretch of being so energized and driven, I never had messages feel coded like this. And I never heard my name when no one was actually there, either. All of those experiences really only started once my mood shifted and my workload got a lot more intense after I started my MBA prerequisites. So before that, no, I didn't think they were coordinating anything for me.
How long have you held this belief that your classmate and the startup advisor are coordinating career opportunities for you?
It's been going on for about two months now. That's when I started taking the part-time MBA prerequisite program, while still working my regular operations job. So, yeah, right around two months.
Do you think the idea that your classmate and startup advisor are coordinating career opportunities for you in this specific way would be considered a normal or common belief by most people?

Honestly, no. I... I know it sounds really hard to explain to anyone else, and that's actually why I came in. I realize that being completely convinced that my classmate and this startup advisor are quietly coordinating opportunities for me—like believing that everyday comments in class or regular Slack messages are these coded signals about where my career is supposed to go—isn't something most people would experience. I know it probably sounds pretty unusual from the outside, even though it feels incredibly real to me.
Do you think your belief about the coded signals would be considered bizarre by a typical person?

Yeah, like I was just saying, I do think it would seem bizarre to most people. I... I came in specifically because I know this sounds hard to explain, but I’ve been completely convinced that one of my MBA classmates and a startup advisor are quietly coordinating opportunities for me. Taking just regular comments in class or normal Slack messages and seeing them as coded signals about where my career is supposed to go... I know that sounds strange. So, yes, I realize a typical person would definitely think it's bizarre.
Do you think the plan you believe your classmate and the startup advisor have for you is highly organized and detailed?

No, not really. I mean, it doesn't feel like some grand, detailed master plan with steps laid out or anything. It's more just... a general feeling that they're guiding me. Like they have an idea of where I should end up, and they're just nudging me in that direction. But I wouldn't say it's highly organized.
